kh:body.core:para: This Practice Note explains the key elements of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012 (UK EMIR) and covers: (1) the clearing obligation, (2) the trade reporting obligation, (3) margin requirements for non-centrally cleared over the counter (OTC) derivatives, and (4) additional risk mitigation requirements for uncleared trades, including timely confirmation, portfolio reconciliation, portfolio compression, and dispute resolution.

Section 1(1) and Schedule 1 Part 1 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 (FSMA 2023) provide for the revocation of UK EMIR with effect from a date or dates to be appointed by HM Treasury. No date has yet been appointed.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Key requirements of UK EMIR
tr:secsub1.core:para: UK EMIR is the principal UK measure regulating the over the counter (OTC) derivatives market. Its key elements are:

core:listitem.core:para: a requirement to clear certain standardised OTC derivatives traded by certain counterparties through a central counterparty (CCP)—see Clearing obligation below
a requirement to report derivative contracts to a trade repository (TR)—see Trade reporting obligation below
margin requirements for non-centrally cleared OTC derivatives traded by certain counterparties—see Margin requirements below, and

additional risk mitigation requirements for uncleared trades, including timely confirmation, portfolio reconciliation, portfolio compression and dispute resolution—see Additional risk mitigation requirements below

tr:secsub1.core:para: Practice Note: UK Regulation of CCPs provides detailed information on the regulatory framework for CCPs set out in UK EMIR.

tr:secsub1.core:title: UK EMIR level 2 and level 3 measures
tr:secsub1.core:para: For an overview of UK EMIR technical standards (TS), see Practice Note: UK EMIR—level 2 and level 3 measures.

tr:secmain.core:title: Derivatives and OTC derivatives
tr:secmain.core:para: Article 2(5) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Regulated Activities) Order 2001, SI 2001/544, Sch 2A derivative contract is a financial instrument set out in paragraphs 4–10 of Part 1 of Schedule 2 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Regulated Activities) Order 2001 (RAO), SI 2001/544.

core:listitem.core:para: options, futures, swaps, forward rate agreements and any other derivative contracts relating to:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: securities, currencies, interest rates or yields, emission allowances, financial indices or financial measures which may be settled physically or in cash
commodities that must be settled in cash or may be settled in cash at the option of one of the parties (other than by reason of a default or other termination event)

commodities that can be physically settled provided that they are traded on a regulated market, a multilateral trading facility (MTF), or an organised trading facility (OTF), except for wholesale energy products traded on an OTF that must be physically settled

climatic variables, freight rates or inflation rates or other official economic statistics that must be settled in cash or may be settled in cash at the option of one of the parties other than by reason of default or other termination even

core:listitem.core:para: derivative instruments for the transfer of credit risk, and
financial contracts for differences

tr:secmain.core:para: An OTC derivative contract is a derivative contract which is not executed on a UK regulated market within the meaning given in Article 2(1)(13A) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 600/2014 (UK MiFIR) or on a third-country market considered to be equivalent to a UK regulated market in accordance with an implementing act adopted by the European Commission under Article 2a of EU EMIR before IP completion day (31 December 2020) or in accordance with regulations made by the HM Treasury under Article 2a of UK EMIR after IP completion day.
The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) maintains a list of third country markets considered equivalent to a UK regulated market for the purposes of UK EMIR.

tr:secsub1.core:title: What is the clearing obligation?
tr:secsub1.core:para: For general information on clearing derivatives, see Practice Note: What is clearing?
The clearing obligation under UK EMIR is a requirement to clear OTC derivative contracts through a CCP which has been authorised or recognised under UK EMIR.

Article 4(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012The clearing obligation applies if, at the time an OTC derivative contract is entered into or novated, it belongs to a class which has been declared subject to the clearing obligation, and:

core:listitem.core:para: both counterparties are established in the UK and subject to the clearing obligation in relation to that class, or

one counterparty is established in the UK and subject to the clearing obligation in relation to that class, and the other counterparty is a third-country entity that would be subject to the clearing obligation if it were established in the UK, or
both counterparties are third-country entities that would be subject to the clearing obligation if they were established in the UK, and either:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: the derivative contract has a direct, substantial and foreseeable effect within the UK, or
the application of the clearing obligation to the derivative contract is necessary or appropriate to prevent the evasion of any provisions of UK EMIR

tr:secsub1.core:title: Which OTC derivative contracts have been declared subject to the clearing obligation?
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 5(2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Regulatory technical standards (RTS) may be made as follows:

core:listitem.core:para: the Bank of England (BoE) may make RTS specifying the class or classes of OTC derivatives that should be subject to the clearing obligation

BoE may make RTS for financial counterparties that are Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA)-authorised persons and the FCA may make RTS for all other cases, specifying the date or dates from which the clearing obligation takes effect, including any phase in and the categories of counterparties to which the obligation applies

tr:secsub1.core:para: As of IP completion day (31 December 2020), the following initial RTS declaring classes of OTC derivatives subject to the clearing obligation applied under UK EMIR:

core:listitem.core:para: Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2015/2205 (as amended by Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (Amendment etc) (EU Exit) (No 2) Instrument 2019)—EUR, GBP, JPY and USD interest rate swaps

Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/592 (as amended by Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (Amendment etc) (EU Exit) (No 2) Instrument 2019)—index credit default swaps, and

Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/1178 (as amended by Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (Amendment etc) (EU Exit) (No 2) Instrument 2019)—NOK, PLN and SEK interest rate swaps

tr:secsub1.core:para: The application of the clearing obligation to the classes of OTC derivatives specified in these RTS was phased in over the dates specified in the RTS, as amended by Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2017/751. The final phase-in date was 9 August 2019.

On 20 May 2021, BoE published Consultation Paper: Derivatives clearing obligation—modifications to reflect interest rate benchmark reform: Amendments to BTS 2015/2205. In this consultation, BoE proposes amendments to Commission Delegated Retained Regulation 2015/2205. These amendments are made by the draft UK technical standards which are set out in the Appendix to the consultation paper.

As a consequence of the anticipated changes in market activity resulting from interest rate benchmark reform, BoE intended to remove contracts that reference benchmarks that are being discontinued and replace them with overnight index swaps (OIS), with the same range of maturities, which reference the replacement risk-free reference rate benchmarks selected for each currency. The changes relate to the benchmarks currently within the scope of the clearing obligation that are being discontinued by January 2022, specifically to remove contracts referencing:

core:listitem.core:para: EONIA and replace them with contracts referencing €STR
referencing JPY LIBOR
GBP LIBOR and replace them with contracts referencing SONIA

tr:secsub1.core:para: As the most widely used USD settings were scheduled to cease in June 2023, the proposed changes did not relate to the transition from USD LIBOR.

On 29 September 2021, BoE published Policy Statement: Derivatives clearing obligation—modifications to reflect interest rate benchmark reform: Amendments to BTS 2015/2205, which sets out BoE’s final policy and maintains the modifications proposed in the May 2021 consultation paper. The Bank Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Clearing Obligation) Instrument 2021, which amends Commission Delegated Retained Regulation 2015/2205 to implement the final policy, is set out in the Appendix to the Policy Statement.
The amendments came into force as follows:

core:listitem.core:para: removing contracts referencing EONIA and replacing them with contracts referencing €STR—18 October 2021
removing contracts refencing JPY LIBOR—6 December 2021
removing contracts referencing GBP LIBOR and replace them with contracts referencing SONIA—20 December 2021

tr:secsub1.core:para: On 29 September 2021, BoE also published Consultation paper: Derivatives clearing obligation—introduction of contracts referencing TONA: Amendment to BTS 2015/2205. This sets out BoE’s proposal to add OIS that reference Tokyo Overnight Average (TONA) to the scope of contracts which are subject to the derivatives clearing obligation.

On 3 December 2021, BoE published Policy Statement Derivatives clearing obligation—introduction of contracts referencing TONA: Amendment to BTS 2015/2205, which sets out BoE’s final policy on the proposal to add OIS that reference TONA to the scope of contracts subject to the derivatives clearing obligation. The final policy maintains the proposal in the September 2021 consultation paper to add TONA OIS contracts with an original maturity between 7 days and 30 years to the clearing obligation. However, the date on which this change comes into force has been postponed from 6 December 2021 to 31 January 2022. The final policy is implemented via amendments to Commission Delegated Retained Regulation (EU) 2015/2205 set out in Bank Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Clearing Obligation) (No. 2) Instrument 2021.

On 9 June 2022, BoE published Derivatives clearing obligation—modifications to reflect USD interest rate benchmark reform: Amendments to BTS 2015/2205 Consultation paper, in which BoE consulted on a proposal to modify the scope of contracts which are subject to the clearing obligation under UK EMIR, by adding OIS that reference SOFR with effect from 31 October 2022 and, subsequently, removing contracts referencing USD LIBOR.

On 24 August 2022, BoE published Policy Statement Derivatives clearing obligation—modifications to reflect USD interest rate benchmark reform: Amendment to BTS 2015/2205, which contains its final policy on the proposal to add OIS that reference the Secured Overnight Funding Rate (SOFR) to the scope of contracts subject to the clearing obligation and to remove contracts referencing USD LIBOR. The final policy maintains the proposal to add SOFR OIS contracts with an original maturity between 7 days and 50 years from 31 October 2022, and to subsequently remove contracts referencing USD LIBOR, and is implemented via amendments to Commission Delegated Retained Regulation (EU) 2015/2205 set out in Bank Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Clearing Obligation) Instrument 2022.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Which counterparties must clear OTC derivative contracts?
tr:secsub1.core:para: With effect from 17 June 2019, the date of application of Regulation (EU) 2019/834 (EMIR REFIT), the rules for determining which market participants are subject to the clearing obligation are as set out below.
Counterparties are categorised as financial counterparties (FCs) or non-financial counterparties (NFCs).
Article 2(8) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012The following are FCs if established in the UK:

core:listitem.core:para: an investment firm within the meaning given in Article 2(1A) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 600/2014 (UK MIFIR) which:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: has its registered office or head office in the UK

has permission under Part 4A of the Financial Services and markets Act 2000 (FSMA 2000) to carry on regulated activities relating to investment services and activities (as defined in Article 2(1)(2) of UK MIFIR) in the UK

would require an authorisation given under MiFID II (as it had effect immediately before IP completion day) if it had its registered office (or if it does not have a registered office, its head office) in an EEA state, and

is not a firm which has permission under FSMA 2000, Pt 4A to carry on regulated activities as an exempt investment firm, within the meaning given in Regulation 8 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Markets in Financial Instruments) Regulations 2017, SI 2017/701

core:listitem.core:para: a credit institution which is a CRR firm (within the meaning given in Article 4(1)(2A) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 575/2013 (UK CRR)
an insurance undertaking or a reinsurance undertaking within the meaning given in FSMA 2000, s 417

a UK UCITS (within the meaning given in FSMA 2000, s 237(3)) and, where relevant, its management company (within the meaning given in FSMA 2000, s 237(2)) unless that UCITS is set up exclusively for the purposes of serving one or more employee share purchase plans
an occupational pension scheme within the meaning given in section 1(1) of the Pension Schemes Act 1993 which is established in the UK

an AIF (within the meaning given in the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Regulations 2013, SI 2013/1773, reg 3) which is either established in the UK or managed by an AIFM (within the meaning given in SI 2013/1773, reg 4) authorised or registered in accordance with SI 2013/1773 unless that AIF is set up exclusively for the purpose of serving one or more employee share purchase plans or unless that AIF is a securitisation special purpose entity as defined in Article 4.1(an) of Directive 2011/61/EU, and where relevant, its AIFM is established in the UK, or
a central securities depository authorised in accordance with Assimilated Regulation (EU) 909/2014 (UK CSDR)

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 2(9) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012An NFC is an undertaking established in the UK which is not an FC.

core:para.core:emph: Calculation of aggregate month-end average position in OTC derivatives—FC+s and NFC+s

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 4a of Regulation (EU) 648/2012Article 4a of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Every 12 months, an FC may calculate its aggregate month-end average position in OTC derivatives (on a group basis and including hedging transactions) for the previous 12 months. An FC is subject to the clearing obligation (an FC+) only if it:

core:listitem.core:para: elects not to calculate its OTC derivatives positions, or
Article 10(4)(b) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012having calculated its OTC derivatives positions, exceeds any of the clearing thresholds specified pursuant to Article 10(4)(b) of UK EMIR

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 4a(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012If an FC elects not to make the calculation, or exceeds any of the clearing thresholds, then it:

core:listitem.core:para: must immediately notify the FCA
must establish clearing arrangements within four months of the notification

becomes subject to the clearing obligation in respect of all OTC derivative contracts belonging to any class of OTC derivatives which is subject to the clearing obligation (not just the class or classes in respect of which the FC has exceeded the clearing threshold) entered into or novated more than four months following the notification

tr:secsub1.core:para: An FC which is not subject to the clearing obligation may be referred to as a small FC, though this is potentially misleading as an FC with small trading volumes would become subject to the clearing obligation if it elected not to make the 12-month calculation of its aggregate month-end average positions.

Article 4a(2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012An FC that was an FC+ on 17 June 2019 under the rules applying before the effectiveness of EMIR REFIT, or becomes an FC+ after 17 June 2019, shall remain an FC+ and continue clearing until it demonstrates to the FCA that its aggregate month-end average position for the previous 12 months does not exceed the clearing threshold.
An FC may therefore potentially become, or cease to be, an FC+ on multiple occasions.

Article 10(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Every 12 months, an NFC which takes positions in OTC derivatives contracts may calculate its aggregate month-end average position in OTC derivatives (on a group basis and excluding hedging transactions and treasury financing transactions) for the previous 12 months. An NFC which takes positions in OTC derivatives contracts is subject to the clearing obligation (an NFC+) only if it:

core:listitem.core:para: elects not to calculate its OTC derivatives positions, or
having calculated its OTC derivatives positions, exceeds any of the clearing thresholds specified pursuant to Article 10(4)(b)

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 0(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012If an NFC elects not to make the calculation, or exceeds any of the clearing thresholds specified pursuant to Article 10(4)(b), then it:

core:listitem.core:para: must immediately notify the FCA
must establish clearing arrangements within four months of the notification, and

becomes subject to the clearing obligation in respect of all OTC derivative contracts pertaining to those asset classes in respect of which the result of the calculation exceeds the clearing thresholds or, where the NFC has not calculated its position, that pertain to any class of OTC derivatives which is subject to the clearing obligation, entered into or novated more than four months following the notification

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 10(2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012An NFC which was an NFC+ on 17 June 2019 under the rules applying before the effectiveness of EMIR REFIT, or which becomes an NFC+ after 17 June 2019, shall remain an NFC+ and continue clearing until it demonstrates to the FCA that its aggregate month-end average position for the previous 12 months does not exceed the clearing threshold.
An NFC may therefore potentially become, or cease to be, an NFC+ on multiple occasions and in respect of various classes of OTC derivatives.

RTS on the EMIR clearing obligation are set out in Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013 (as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No 2) Instrument 2019 (FCA 2019/62)).
These RTS specify:

core:listitem.core:para: criteria for treating OTC derivatives as being used to hedge commercial activity or treasury financing, and
clearing thresholds for OTC derivatives for the purposes of Article 10(4)(b) of UK EMIR

tr:secsub1.core:para: The clearing thresholds for OTC derivatives for the purposes of Article 10(4)(b) of UK EMIR are set out in the table below:

row.entry: OTC commodity derivative contracts and other OTC derivative contracts not expressly provided for

tr:secsub1.core:title: Third-country counterparties
tr:secsub1.core:para: RTS on the application of the UK EMIR clearing obligation to third-country counterparties are set out in Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 285/2014 (as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (Amendment etc) (EU Exit) (No 2) Instrument 2019).

Article 2(1) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 285/2014 (as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (Amendment etc) (EU Exit) (No 2) Instrument 2019)An OTC derivative contract shall be considered as having a direct, substantial and foreseeable effect within the UK when at least one third-country entity benefits from a guarantee provided by an FC established in the UK which covers all or part of its liability resulting from the derivative contract, if the guarantee meets the following conditions:

core:listitem.core:para: it is for an amount of at least €8bn or the equivalent in another currency, and
it is at least equal to 5% of the sum of current exposures in OTC derivatives contracts of the FC established in the UK issuing the guarantee

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 2(2) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 285/2014 (as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (Amendment etc) (EU Exit) (No 2) Instrument 2019)An OTC derivative contract shall be considered as having a direct, substantial and foreseeable effect within the UK where the two entities established in a third country enter into the OTC derivative contract through their branches in the UK and would qualify as FCs if they were established in the UK.

Article 3(1) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 285/2014An OTC derivative contract shall be deemed to have been designed to circumvent the application of any provision of UK EMIR if the way in which that contract has been concluded is considered, when viewed as a whole and having regard to all the circumstances, to have as its primary purpose the avoidance of the application of any provision of UK EMIR.

Article 3(2) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 285/2014An OTC derivative contract shall be considered as having for its primary purpose the avoidance of the application of any provision of UK EMIR if the primary purpose of the contract or any related arrangements is to defeat the object, spirit and purpose of any provision of UK EMIR that would otherwise apply. This includes a situation where the contract is part of an artificial arrangement or artificial series of arrangements.

Article 3(2) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 285/2014An arrangement that intrinsically lacks business rationale, commercial substance or relevant economic justification and consists of any contract, transaction, scheme, action, operation, agreement, grant, understanding, promise, undertaking or event shall be considered an artificial arrangement. The arrangement may comprise more than one step or part.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Intragroup exemption
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 4(2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012OTC derivative contracts that are intragroup transactions are not subject to the UK EMIR clearing obligation.
Article 3(2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012In relation to an FC, an intragroup transaction is any of the following:

core:listitem.core:para: an OTC derivative contract entered into with another counterparty which is part of the same group, provided that the following conditions are met:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: the FC is established in the UK or, if it is established in a third country, the Commission has adopted an implementing act under Article 13(2) of EU EMIR recognising the equivalence of the regulatory regime of that third country before IP completion day or HM Treasury has made regulations under that Article13(2) of UK EMIR in respect of that third country after IP completion day (a UK EMIR equivalent third country)
the other counterparty is a financial counterparty, a financial holding company, a financial institution or an ancillary services undertaking subject to appropriate prudential requirements
both counterparties are included in full in the same consolidation, and
both counterparties are subject to appropriate centralised risk evaluation, measurement and control procedures

core:listitem.core:para: an OTC derivative contract entered into with an NFC which is part of the same group provided that both counterparties are included in the same consolidation on a full basis and they are subject to an appropriate centralised risk evaluation, measurement and control procedures and that counterparty is established in the UK or in a UK EMIR equivalent third country

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 3(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012In relation to an NFC, an intragroup transaction is an OTC derivative contract entered into with another counterparty which is part of the same group provided that both counterparties are included in the same consolidation in full and they are subject to an appropriate centralised risk evaluation, measurement and control procedures and that counterparty is established in the UK or a UK EMIR equivalent third country.

Over the Counter Derivatives, Central Counterparties and Trade Repositories (Amendment, etc, and Transitional Provision) (EU Exit) Regulations, SI 2019/335, regs 80–81The Over the Counter Derivatives, Central Counterparties and Trade Repositories (Amendment, etc, and Transitional Provision) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 SI 2019/335, regs 80–81, establish a temporary intragroup regime which provides that intragroup transactions which were exempt from the EU EMIR clearing requirements before IP completion day continue to be exempted from the clearing requirements in UK EMIR. Under this regime, the UK EMIR clearing obligation will apply to such an intragroup transaction entered into between a counterparty established in the UK and one established in a third country (including an EEA Member State) as follows:

core:listitem.core:para: from 1 January 2024 (or, if applicable, a later date determined by HM Treasury), where no equivalence decision has been adopted by HM Treasury in relation to the third country, or
the later of the following dates where an equivalence decision has been adopted:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: 60 days after the date of entry into force of the equivalence decision, and
the date when the clearing obligation applies to the counterparties

tr:secsub1.core:para: On 9 November 2020, HM Treasury published The European Market Infrastructure Regulation (Article 13) Equivalence Directions 2020 which grant partial equivalence to the EEA Member States under Article 13 of UK EMIR in relation to intragroup exemptions from the clearing obligation for uncleared derivative transactions. This direction took effect immediately following the end of the transition period. In practice, this means that intragroup exemptions for trades between UK and EEA group entities under the temporary intragroup regime expired on 1 March 2021. However, the direction allows firms to apply for intra-group exemptions with no expiry date. Information on the application process may be found on the FCA’s EMIR news webpage.

On 28 March 2023, HMT published Guidance Extending the pension fund clearing exemption and exemptions for intragroup transactions, in which HMT announced that it intended to lay a statutory instrument extending the exemption for pension funds from the clearing obligation by a period of two years and extending the temporary intragroup exemption regime by a further three years. The statutory instrument would amend Article 89 (1) of UK EMIR and the relevant days set out in Articles 81(1)(b), 81(2)(b), 83(1)(b) and 83(2)(b) of The Over the Counter Derivatives, Central Counterparties and Trade Repositories (Amendment, etc, and Transitional Provision) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/335. The Pension Fund Clearing Obligation Exemption and Intragroup Transaction Transitional Clearing and Risk-Management Obligation Exemptions (Extension and Amendment) Regulations 2023, SI 2023/472, were laid on 27 April 2023 and have effect from 12 June 2023.

On 5 November 2025, HMT published Draft Statutory Instrument—The Over the Counter Derivatives (Intragroup Transactions) Regulations 2026 and related Policy Note, with the purpose of widening the availability of permanent intragroup exemptions for margin and clearing given their usual risk management function, while ensuring that the use of these exemptions is still subject to robust monitoring and approval by the financial services regulators (by altering the requirements for an intragroup transaction in Article 3 of UK EMIR, so that it no longer links to equivalence decisions under Article 13 of UK EMIR), and streamlining the intragroup exemption process for margin and clearing to make it simpler and faster for firms to obtain and use exemptions (amending Articles 4 and 11 of UK EMIR).

Also on 5 November 2025, the FCA published CP25/30 Streamlining the UK EMIR Intragroup Regime. The FCA proposes changes to Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 and Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013 to support HMT’s reforms. Among other things, the changes will reduce the supplementary documents required for intragroup exemptions from the bilateral margin requirements simplify the process for counterparties, making it easier to navigate the requirements of the UK EMIR Intragroup Regime for margin exemptions.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Exemption for pension funds
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 89(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012OTC derivative contracts that are objectively measurable as reducing investment risks directly relating to the financial solvency of pension scheme arrangements (PSAs) were exempt from the clearing obligation for a transitional period. (As mentioned below, this exemption has now been made permanent).
Article 89(1) of Regulation (EU) 648/2012EMIR REFIT extended the transitional period for pension schemes to 18 June 2021.

Article 89(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012The exemption for PSAs was initially maintained under UK EMIR, for both UK and EEA funds, until 18 June 2023. HM Treasury is empowered to further extend the exemption by up to two years at a time if it concludes that no appropriate technical solution has been developed for the transfer by UK and EU PSAs of cash and non-cash collateral as variation margins and that the adverse effect of centrally clearing derivative contracts on the retirement benefits of future pensioners remains.

On 28 March 2023, HMT published Guidance Extending the pension fund clearing exemption and exemptions for intragroup transactions, in which HMT announced that it intended to lay a statutory instrument extending the exemption for pension funds from the clearing obligation by a period of two years and extending the temporary intragroup exemption regime by a further three years. The statutory instrument would amend Article 89 (1) of UK EMIR and the relevant days set out in Articles 81(1)(b), 81(2)(b), 83(1)(b) and 83(2)(b) of The Over the Counter Derivatives, Central Counterparties and Trade Repositories (Amendment, etc., and Transitional Provision) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/335. The Pension Fund Clearing Obligation Exemption and Intragroup Transaction Transitional Clearing and Risk-Management Obligation Exemptions (Extension and Amendment) Regulations 2023, SI 2023/472 were laid on 27 April 2023 and have effect from 12 June 2023.

On 13 November 2023, HMT published Call for evidence: pension fund clearing exemption, in which HMT sought input from industry stakeholders on pension funds’ exemption from the clearing obligation, to inform the government’s long-term approach.

On 10 January 2025, HMT published Pension fund clearing exemption Call for evidence response. The government has decided to maintain the exemption for the longer term. Legislation will be introduced to prevent the exemption's expiration on 18 June 2025 and remove any further time limit.
On 18 March 2025, a draft of The Pension Fund Clearing Obligation Exemption (Amendment) Regulations 2025 was published, together with a draft Explanatory Memorandum.

The Pension Fund Clearing Obligation Exemption (Amendment) Regulations 2025, SI 2025/670, were made on 10 June 2025 and came into force on 11 June 2025. SI 2025/670 makes the transitional exemption permanent.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Exemption for covered bond entities and SSPEs
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 4(5) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012OTC derivative contracts entered into by covered bond entities in connection with a covered bond, or by a securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) in connection with a securitisation, are exempt from the clearing obligation provided that:

core:listitem.core:para: in the case of an SSPE, the SSPE issues only securitisations that meet the requirements for simple, transparent and standardised (STS) securitisations under Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2017/2402 (UK Securitisation Regulation) and including securitisations notified as STS in accordance with Article 27 of the EU Securitisation Regulation before IP completion day, or before the expiry of a period of two years beginning with IP completion day, where the person responsible for the notification (the originator and sponsor or, in the case of an ABCP programme, the sponsor) is established in an EEA State
the OTC derivative contract is used only to hedge interest rate or currency mismatches under the covered bond or securitisation, and

the arrangements under the covered bond or securitisation adequately mitigate counterparty credit risk with respect to the OTC derivative contracts concluded by the covered bond entity or SSPE special purpose entity in connection with the covered bond or securitisation

tr:secsub1.core:para: RTS on the specification of criteria for establishing the arrangements to adequately mitigate counterparty credit risk associated with covered bonds and securitisations are set out in Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2020/447.
For information on STS securitisations, see Practice Note: UK Securitisation Regulation—essentials [Archived]—STS securitisations.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Proposed exemption for post-trade risk reduction transactions
tr:secsub1.core:para: On 11 December 2025, BoE published Exempting post-trade risk reduction transactions from the clearing obligation Consultation Paper.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Suspension of the clearing obligation
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 6a(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012BoE may, with the consent of HM Treasury, direct that the clearing obligation referred be suspended for specific classes of OTC derivatives or for a specific type of counterparty if one of the following conditions is met:

core:listitem.core:para: the specific classes of OTC derivatives are no longer suitable for central clearing in accordance with the criteria referred to in Articles 5(4) and (5) of UK EMIR
a CCP is likely to cease clearing those specific classes of OTC derivatives and no other CCP is able to clear those specific classes of OTC derivatives without interruption

the suspension of the clearing obligation for those specific classes of OTC derivatives or for a specific type of counterparty is necessary to avoid or address a serious threat to financial stability or to the orderly functioning of financial markets in the UK and the suspension is proportionate to those aims

tr:secsub1.core:para: BoE must inform the FCA of its intention to make a direction as soon as is reasonably practicable after making the decision to make a direction.

Article 6a(2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012The FCA may inform BoE that, in its opinion, there is evidence that one of the conditions for suspension of the clearing obligation has been met. BoE shall consider the FCA's information, and respond as appropriate within a reasonable time from the receipt of that information.

Article 6a(3) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012A direction under Article 6a(1) of UK EMIR to suspend the clearing obligation for specific classes of OTC derivatives shall also trigger a suspension of the trading obligation laid down in Article 28(1) and (2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 for the same classes of OTC derivatives that are subject to the suspension of the clearing obligation.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Regulatory regime for CCPs
tr:secsub1.core:para: The mandatory clearing requirement eliminates counterparty risk for the transactions which are cleared, but substitutes CCP risk. The use of the relatively small number of CCPs to clear standardised derivatives concentrates risk in CCPs and creates a new potential source of risk to the financial system as a whole.
UK EMIR contains provisions which are intended to avoid CCP failure by ensuring that CCPs are financially resilient, covering:

core:listitem.core:para: management of CCPs’ exposures to their clearing members
margin management
the capital that CCPs are required to hold
default funds, additional resources and default waterfalls
the risk that a CCP’s financial resources will not be available to it quickly enough to allow it to meet a sudden default by a major clearing member, known as liquidity risk
the types of collateral that CCPs may accept for margin purposes
the ways in which a CCP may invest its financial resources

the way in which a CCP deals with defaults by its clearing members, including porting, which is transferring the assets and positions which a defaulting clearing member holds on behalf of its clients to another clearing member or members selected by the clients, and
review, stress testing and back testing of the models underlying CCP exposure and risk management

tr:secsub1.core:para: UK EMIR also sets out requirements for:

core:listitem.core:para: identification and management of conflicts of interest between a CCP and its clearing members or their clients known to the CCP
establishment of a business continuity policy and disaster recovery plan
interoperability between CCPs
segregation and portability of client assets

tr:secsub1.core:para: FSMA 2023 introduces a general rule-making power for the BoE in relation CCPs and CSDs, so that it can take on primary responsibility for setting regulatory requirements for these entities. In addition, FSMA 2023:

core:listitem.core:para: updates the framework that sits around this power in order to strengthen the BoE’s accountability to Parliament, its relationship with HMT and its engagement with stakeholders

provides the BoE with a power to impose requirements on individual CCPs and CSDs, similar to the FCA and PRA’s ability to impose requirements on the firms they regulate under FSMA 2000, ss 55L and 55M

establishes the concept of a ‘systemic third-country CCP’, which the BoE can decide should be subject to the domestic rulebook—HMT may grant the BoE further powers to apply domestic rules to non-systemic overseas CCPs and CSDs as well, should it deem it necessary in the future, and
provides for the revocation of the relevant CCP provisions within UK EMIR (on a date to be appointed)

tr:secsub1.core:para: For information on the regulation of CCPs, see Practice Note: UK Regulation of CCPs.

tr:secsub1.core:title: What is the trade reporting obligation?
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 9(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012The trade reporting obligation is a requirement for UK firms and CCPs:to report the details of any derivative contract entered into, modified or terminated to a TR which has been registered or recognised under UK EMIR.

tr:secsub1.core:title: What derivatives does the trade reporting obligation apply to?
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 9(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012With effect from 17 June 2019, the date of application of EMIR REFIT, the reporting obligation applies to all derivatives which:

core:listitem.core:para: were entered into before 12 February 2014 and remained outstanding on that date, or
were entered into on or after 12 February 2014

tr:secsub1.core:para: Unlike the clearing obligation, the trade reporting obligation is not limited to OTC derivative contracts and applies to exchange traded derivative contracts—see Derivatives and OTC derivatives for the definition of derivatives.

Article 9(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012With effect from 17 June 2019, the date of application of EU EMIR REFIT, there is an exemption for intragroup transactions—the trade reporting obligation does not apply to derivative contracts within the same group if:

core:listitem.core:para: at least one of the counterparties is an NFC or would be qualified as an NFC if it were established in the UK
both counterparties are included in the same consolidation on a full basis
both counterparties are subject to appropriate centralised risk evaluation, measurement and control procedures, and
the parent undertaking is not an FC

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 9(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012A counterparty which intends to rely on the intragroup exemption is required to notify the FCA

tr:secsub1.core:title: What must be reported?
tr:secsub1.core:para: Annex to Commission Assimilated Delegated Regulation (EU) 148/2013The information to be reported is set out in the Annex to Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 148/2013 (as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No 2) Instrument 2019 (FCA 2019/62)).

Further detailed reporting requirements are set out in Commission Implementing Assimilated Regulation (EU) 1247/2012 (as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No 2) Instrument 2019 (FCA 2019/62)).
UK reporting counterparties and UK TRs should use the UK EMIR validation rules (available here) when submitting derivative transactions entered into from 11 pm on 31 December 2020 onwards.

Article 3(4) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 148/2013FCs and NFC+s must report mark-to-market or mark-to-model valuations and collateral value (on a transaction or portfolio basis).
The FCA’s UK EMIR News webpage includes information on reporting an amendment to a reference rate or the application of a fallback in place of LIBOR.

tr:secsub1.core:title: When does the report need to be made?
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 9(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Article 2 of Commission Implementing Assimilated Regulation (EU) 1247/2012 as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No.2) Instrument 2019 (FCA 2019/62)The details must be reported as they occur, except that mark-to-market or mark-to-model valuations of contracts must be reported on a daily basis. In all cases, reports must be made no later than the working day following the conclusion, modification or termination of the contract.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Who is required to report?
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 9(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Each counterparty to a derivative contract is subject to the reporting obligation and must report each derivative contract except that:

core:listitem.core:para: Article 9(1a) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012FCs are solely responsible for reporting on behalf of both counterparties, the details of OTC derivative contracts concluded with an NFC which is not an NFC+, although an NFC may opt to retain responsibility for reporting

Article 9(1a) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012an NFC which is not an NFC+ and which enters into an OTC derivative contract with an entity established in a third country is not required to report if:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: the third-country entity would be qualified as an FC if it were established in the UK
the legal regime for reporting to which the third-country entity is subject has been declared equivalent pursuant to Article 13 of UK EMIR, and

the third-country FC has reported under the third-country reporting regime to a TR that is subject to a legally binding and enforceable obligation to grant the entities referred to in Article 81(3) of UK EMIR (which include the FCA, BoE and the Pensions Regulator) direct and immediate access to the data

core:listitem.core:para: Article 9(1b) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012the management company of a UCITS is responsible for reporting the details of OTC derivative contracts to which that UCITS is a counterparty
Article 9(1c) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012an AIFM is responsible for reporting the details of OTC derivative contracts entered into by an AIF that it manages

Article 9(1d) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012the trustees or managers of an occupational pension scheme (within the meaning given in Section 1(1) of the Pension Schemes Act 1993) are responsible for reporting the details of OTC derivative contracts to which that occupational pension scheme is a counterparty

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 9(1) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012UK CCPs are also subject to the trade reporting obligation.

Article 9(3) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Except where the FCA has suspended the reporting obligation under Article 9(3A) of UK EMIR, where a trade repository is not available to record the details of a derivative contract:

core:listitem.core:para: counterparties and CCPs shall ensure that such details are reported to the FCA, and

the FCA shall ensure that all the relevant entities referred to in Article 81(3) of UK EMIR have access to all the details of derivative contracts they need to fulfil their respective responsibilities and mandates

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 9(3A) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012The FCA may suspend the reporting obligation. Before it does so it must:

core:listitem.core:para: provide a report to HM Treasury setting out its reasons for suspending the reporting obligation
specify a date:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: on which the suspension of the reporting obligation will end
by which it anticipates counterparties and CCPs will be able to report details of any derivative contracts as set out in Article 9(3) of UK EMIR, and

core:listitem.core:para: consult HM Treasury and BoE

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 9(3B) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012The FCA may, with the consent of HM Treasury, suspend the reporting obligation under Article 9(3A) of UK EMIR for a period of up to one year or such longer period as HM Treasury may by regulations specify.

Article 9(3C) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Details of any derivative contracts that counterparties and CCPs have concluded, and of any modification or termination of the contract, that have not been reported to a trade must be reported by those counterparties and CCPs to a trade repository following the end of the suspension of the reporting obligation by no later than the end of the period specified by the FCA for this purpose.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Regulatory regime for TRs
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 55 of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012UK TRs are required to register with the FCA. To be eligible to be registered, a trade repository must be a legal person established in the UK.
Article 77 of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012A third-country TR may apply for recognition by the FCA if it is authorised and subject to effective supervision in a third country which has:

core:listitem.core:para: been recognised by regulations made by HM Treasury as one in which the arrangements for TRs are equivalent to those in the UK

has entered into co-operation arrangements to provide for the FCA to have immediate and continuous access to the information needed for the performance of its duties, including information on derivative contracts held in trade repositories established in the third country

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 78(9) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012 as added by Retained Regulation (EU) 2019/834TRs are required to establish:

core:listitem.core:para: procedures for the effective reconciliation of data between TRs
procedures to verify the completeness and correctness of the data reported, and
policies for the orderly transfer of data to other TRs repositories where requested by the counterparties or CCPs referred to in Article 9 of UK EMIR or where otherwise necessary

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 81 of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012TRs are required to make information available to authorities and regulators including the FCA, BoE and the Pensions Regulator.

On 5 September 2022, the FCA sent a first portfolio letter to TRs and securitisation repositories outlining its view of the key risks of harm in the sector and what it expects repositories to do to minimise potential risks to market integrity resulting from failures to meet their regulatory requirements or failures to facilitate their customers meeting their UK reporting obligations. The letter also sets out what the FCA is doing to supervise repositories in the portfolio.

tr:secsub1.core:title: FCA and BoE final rules and guidance on changes to the reporting requirements, procedures for data quality and registration of TRs under UK EMIR
tr:secsub1.core:para: On 25 November 2021, FCA and the BoE published joint Consultation Paper CP21/31 Changes to reporting requirements, procedures for data quality and registration of Trade Repositories under UK EMIR.
The changes proposed in CP21/31:

core:listitem.core:para: would be delivered by amending the relevant onshored technical standards and introducing new rules for TRs
aim to align the UK derivatives reporting framework with CPMI-IOSCO’s guidance to ensure a ‘more globally consistent data set’, which will facilitate monitoring systemic and financial stability risk

include measures for mandatory delegated reporting requirements, counterparty notifications and reconciliations processes, the use of XML schemas and global identifiers (intended to provide clarity to counterparties and TRs, including where there are discrepancies on how certain data fields are reported), and
contain new proposed FCA rules for TRs on the registration and reconciliation processes aimed to streamline the process for registration

tr:secsub1.core:para: On 24 February 2023, the FCA and BoE published Policy Statement PS23/2, Changes to reporting requirements, procedures for data quality and registration of trade repositories under UK EMIR—feedback on CP21/31 and our final rules and guidance. PS23/2 includes:

core:listitem.core:para: The Technical Standards (EMIR Reporting and Data Quality and Miscellaneous Amendments) Instrument 2023 (FCA 2023/4), which:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: revokes Commission Implementing Assimilated Regulation (EU) 1247/2012 and Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 148/2013, except as they apply to CCPs
makes the Technical Standards on the Minimum Details of the Data to be Reported to Trade Repositories (Annex A)
makes the Technical Standards on the Standards, Formats, Frequency and Methods and Arrangements for Reporting (Annex B)
amends Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013 (Annexes C and D)
amends Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 151/2013 (Annex E)
amends Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/957 (Annex F)

core:listitem.core:para: The Technical Standards (EMIR Registration of Trade Repositories and Miscellaneous Amendments) Instrument 2023 (FCA 2023/5), which amends:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 150/2013 (Annex A)
Commission Implementing Assimilated Regulation (EU) 1248/2012 (Annex B)
Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 151/2013 (Annex C)

core:listitem.core:para: EMIR Rules (Procedures for Ensuring Data Quality) Instrument 2023 (FCA 2023/3), which makes the European Market Infrastructure Regulation Rules sourcebook (EMIRR)

tr:secsub1.core:para: These changes came into effect on 30 September 2024, except for certain amendments to Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 150/2013 and Commission Implementing Assimilated Regulation (EU) 1248/2012, which relate to the format and details of applications for registration of trade repositories and which came into force on 24 February 2023. There is a six-month period for counterparties to update their outstanding derivative reports in line with the new requirements, which will end on 31 March 2025.

On 1 March 2024, the FCA published Changes to UK EMIR reporting requirements: draft questions and answers. In which, the FCA (alongside BoE) sought feedback on draft guidance (in the form of Q&As) for reporting under the revised UK EMIR Article 9 reporting requirements set out on PS23/2.
Final Q&As relating to the arrangements for transitioning to the updated derivative reporting framework under UK EMIR during the period from 30 September 2024 to 31 March 2025 may be found here.
On 12 July 2024, the FCA consulted on a further question under topic 10.

On 4 September 2024, the FCA published UK EMIR Trade Repositories: draft questions and answers, in which the FCA consulted on guidance (in the form of Questions and Answers) to support TRs in the implementation of the updated UK EMIR reporting requirements that apply from 30 September 2024.

tr:secmain.core:title: Margin requirements
tr:secmain.core:para: Margin requirements are set out in UK EMIR and in Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No.3) Instrument 2019 and the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure Regulation) (EU Exit) (No.5) Instrument 2020 (the UK Margin RTS).

On 9 March 2021, the PRA and FCA published PRA CP6/21/FCA CP21/7—Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives: Amendments to BTS 2016/2251, which sets out proposed amendments to the UK Margin RTS. These amendments are made in the technical standards set out in the appendices to PS14/21 | CP6/21—Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives: Amendments to BTS 2016/2251, which apply from 30 June 2021:

core:para.core:url: PRA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021
FCA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021

tr:secmain.core:para: On 12 July 2022, the PRA and FCA published PRA CP11/22 FCA CP22/13—Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives: Amendments to BTS 2016/2251, which sets out proposals to amend the UK Margin RTS to:

core:listitem.core:para: specify the treatment of third-country funds as eligible collateral, including EEA UCITS
provide a fall-back transition period to address practical issues where firms face immediate application of the bilateral margining requirements, and
update the criteria for a CCP to be excluded from the requirements

tr:secmain.core:para: On 15 December 2022, the PRA and FCA published PRA Policy Statement 11/22 FCA Policy Statement 22/16—Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives: Amendments to BTS 2016/2251, which sets out the regulators’ final policy in the form of amendments to binding technical standards (BTS) 2016/2251 and feedback to responses to their joint consultation paper (PRA CP11/22 and FCA CP22/13). Following industry feedback, the final policy includes minor changes to the proposals consulted on. The changes are made in PRA Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margening) Instrument 2022 and FCA Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margening) Instrument 2022and are effective from the publication date of the joint policy statement.

In PRA CP6/24—Occasional consultation paper: April 2024 and FCA CP24/10: Joint PRA and FCA Consequential Amendments to BTS 2016/2251, published on 30 April 2024, the PRA and FCA consult on proposed consequential amendments to Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 to reflect the expected changes to Article 4 and 11 of UK EMIR that will be made in the draft Securitisation (Amendment) Regulations 2024, such that firms are able to apply the same margining treatment to specified overseas STS securitisations that they would otherwise apply to UK notified STS securitisations.

tr:secsub1.core:title: What are the UK EMIR margin requirements?
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 11(3) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Article 2(1) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251Counterparties may be required to exchange two types of margin (collateral):

core:listitem.core:para: Article 1(2) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251variation margin (VM), and
Article 1(1) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251initial margin (IM)

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 1(2) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251VM reflects the size of the current exposure of the derivative transaction. It changes over time as its value is dependent on the current mark-to-market value of the derivative. Its purpose is to protect transacting parties from the exposure incurred from changes in the mark-to-market value of the derivative transaction.

Article 12 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251VM should be calculated and exchanged subject to a single, legally enforceable netting agreement with sufficient frequency (eg daily).

Article 1(1) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251IM is an amount of collateral (in the form of cash or in some cases eligible securities) exchanged at the time the derivative is entered into. It protects the parties from the potential future exposure that could arise from changes in the mark-to-market value of that transaction during the expected time between the last VM exchange and the liquidation of positions on the default of a counterparty. IM therefore reflects potential future exposure.
The amount of IM deposited depends on different factors, including:

core:listitem.core:para: how often the contract is revalued and VM exchanged, and
how volatile the relevant instrument is

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 9(2) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251IM is paid at the outset of a transaction and thereafter calculated and collected on a routine and consistent basis dependent upon the changes in measured potential future exposure.

Article 9(2) of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251Article 11(1)(b) of Regulation (EU) 648/2012Article 9(2) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251Article 11(1)(b) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012The collection of the IM must be based upon approved models of calculation and parties should ensure that they have rigorous dispute resolution procedures in place before the onset of a transaction.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Which counterparties are subject to the margin requirements?
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 11(3) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012FCs and NFC+s are subject to the margin requirements.

Article 39 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No.3) Instrument 2019For the purposes of the phasing in of the margin requirements, FCs and NFC+s are categorised on the basis of their aggregate average notional amount (AANA) of non-centrally cleared OTC derivative contracts. AANA is to be calculated quarterly on a group basis and to include all non-centrally cleared OTC derivative contracts, including intragroup transactions.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Which transactions do the margin requirements apply to?
tr:secsub1.core:para: The margin requirements apply to all non-centrally cleared OTC derivative contracts, with these exceptions:

core:listitem.core:para: Articles 27(a) and (b) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 PRA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021FCA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021 physically-settled foreign exchange (FX) forwards and FX swaps—no IM, VM only, but the requirement to exchange VM applies only if one of the counterparties is an ‘institution’ as defined in Article 4(1)(3) of UK CRR) (or a third-country firm which would meet the definition of ‘institution’ if established in the UK)
Article 27(c) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 currency swaps—VM only, no IM

Article 38(1) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No.3) Instrument 2019PRA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021FCA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021PRA Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2023FCA Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2023single stock equity options or index options—the margin requirements were to apply from 4 January 2026 but in PS23/25 – Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives: Amendments to BTS 2016/2251 published on 27 November 2025, the PRA and FCA made this exemption permanent
Article 30 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 covered bond hedging swaps—conditions need to be met, if so, only VM to covered bond entity
Recital 5 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 one-way obligations (eg options)—one-way margin

tr:secsub1.core:title: Phase-in of the margin requirements
tr:secsub1.core:para: On 3 April 2020, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) and the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) announced that they had agreed to extend by one year the deadline for completing the final two implementation phases of the margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives (Phases 5 and 6). This is due to the significant challenges posed by the coronavirus (COVID-19), including the displacement of staff and the need for firms to focus resources on managing risks associated with current market volatility. Implementation of this extension would require a further amendment to the Margin RTS. The extended dates are reflected in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/236 and the above table. Corresponding changes have been made to the UK Margin RTS.

Articles 36 and 37 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 The phase-in dates for VM and IM are set out in Articles 36 and 37 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 and are shown in the table below:

row.entry: Phase 5–1 September 2021 (changed from 1 September 2020 by PRA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021 and FCA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021)

Both counterparties have AANA above €50bn (changed from €8bn by PRA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021 and FCA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021)
Phase 6–1 September 2022 (added byPRA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021 and FCA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021)
Both counterparties have AANA above €8bn (added by PRA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021 and FCA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021)

tr:secsub1.core:para: The changes to the phase-in dates for IM set out in PRA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021 and FCA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021 reflect BCBS and IOSCO’s 3 April 2020 announcement that they had agreed to extend by one year the deadline for completing the final two implementation phases of the margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives (Phases 5 and 6).
In CP5/25 – Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives: Amendments to BTS 2016/2251, published on 27 March 2025, the PRA and FCA propose to make the following changes:

core:listitem.core:para: remove the obligation to exchange IM on outstanding legacy contracts, where a firm subsequently falls below the in-scope thresholds, and

permit UK firms, when transacting with a counterparty subjected to the margin requirements in another jurisdiction, to use that jurisdiction’s threshold assessment calculation periods and entry into scope dates to determine whether those transactions are subject to IM requirements

tr:secsub1.core:title: Intragroup exemptions from margin requirements
tr:secsub1.core:para: Articles 3(1) and (2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Intragroup transactions as defined in Articles 3(1) and (2) of UK EMIR—see: ‘Intragroup exemption’ under Clearing obligation—are exempt from the margin requirements, subject to additional conditions.

Article 11(5) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012For an intragroup transaction entered into by counterparties which are established in the UK, the additional condition is that there is no current or foreseen practical or legal impediment to the prompt transfer of own funds or repayment of liabilities between counterparties.

Article 11(8) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012An intragroup transaction referred to in Article 3(2)(a) to (d) of UK EMIR entered into between a counterparty established in the UK and one established in a third country, shall be exempt totally or partially on the basis of a positive decision of the relevant competent authority responsible for supervision of the counterparty which is established in the UK on condition that:

core:listitem.core:para: the risk-management procedures of the counterparties are adequately sound, robust and consistent with the level of complexity of the derivative transaction, and
there is no current or foreseen practical or legal impediment to the prompt transfer of own funds or repayment of liabilities between counterparties

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 11(9) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012An intragroup transaction referred to in Article 3(1) of UK EMIR that is entered into by an NFC which is established in the UK and a counterparty which is established in a third-country jurisdiction shall be exempt on condition that:

core:listitem.core:para: the risk-management procedures of the counterparties are adequately sound, robust and consistent with the level of complexity of the derivative transaction, and
there is no current or foreseen practical or legal impediment to the prompt transfer of own funds or repayment of liabilities between counterparties

tr:secsub1.core:para: SI 2019/335, reg 80There is a transitional regime under which intragroup transactions which were exempt from the margin requirements under EU EMIR before IP completion day are exempted from the margin requirements under UK EMIR. This regime lasts three years and may be extended by HM Treasury.

This means that the margin requirements apply to such an intragroup transaction entered into between a counterparty established in the UK and one established in a third country (including an EEA Member State, but note that an equivalence decision has been adopted for EEA Member States, effective from IP completion day as follows:

core:listitem.core:para: from 1 January 2024 (or, if applicable, a later date determined by HM Treasury), where no equivalence decision has been adopted by HM Treasury in relation to the third country, or
the later of the following dates where an equivalence decision has been adopted:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: 60 days after the date of entry into force of the equivalence decision, and
the date when the clearing obligation applies to the counterparties

tr:secsub1.core:para: SI 2019/335, regs 13, 80SI 2020/1385, reg 52In addition, there is no requirement for UK firms who previously benefitted from intragroup exemptions from margin exemptions with their EEA group entities to re-apply to the FCA. However, as intragroup exemptions from margin granted to UK firms with their third-country group entities where no equivalence has been determined formally expired in January 2020 and have been permitted since then by the FCA on a supervisory basis, firms will be required to re-apply for those exemptions in order to benefit from the transitional regime.

To avoid an unnecessary administrative burden on firms, the FCA adopted a streamlined process for firms that are required to apply for these new exemptions. As set out in Requirements and directions under Regulations 8(4) and (7) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Over the Counter Derivatives, etc) Regulations 2013, SI 2013/504, no more information was required of a firm to complete an application unless:

core:listitem.core:para: circumstances relevant to the satisfaction of exemption conditions have changed (and have not already been communicated to the FCA), or
the counterparty requires individual communication of the decision

tr:secsub1.core:para: On 28 March 2023, HMT published Guidance Extending the pension fund clearing exemption and exemptions for intragroup transactions, in which HMT announced that it intended to lay a statutory instrument extending the exemption for pension funds from the clearing obligation by a period of two years and extending the temporary intragroup exemption regime by a further three years. The statutory instrument would amend Article 89 (1) of UK EMIR and the relevant days set out in Articles 81(1)(b), 81(2)(b), 83(1)(b) and 83(2)(b) of The Over the Counter Derivatives, Central Counterparties and Trade Repositories (Amendment, etc., and Transitional Provision) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/335. The Pension Fund Clearing Obligation Exemption and Intragroup Transaction Transitional Clearing and Risk-Management Obligation Exemptions (Extension and Amendment) Regulations 2023, SI 2023/472, were laid on 27 April 2023 and have effect from 12 June 2023.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Exemptions from margin requirements for covered bond issuers and SSPEs
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 30 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 A counterparty entering into an OTC derivative contract with a covered bond issuer may agree that VM is not posted by the covered bond issuer or cover pool, that VM is posted by the counterparty in the form of cash only, and that neither party posts IM, if:

core:listitem.core:para: the OTC derivative contract is not terminated in case of resolution or insolvency of the covered bond issuer or cover pool
the counterparty ranks at least pari passu with the covered bond holders except where the counterparty is the defaulting or the affected party, or waives the pari passu ranking
the OTC derivative contract is registered or recorded in the cover pool of the covered bond in accordance with national covered bond legislation
the derivative contract is used only to hedge the interest rate or currency mismatches of the cover pool in relation to the covered bond
the netting set does not include OTC derivative contracts unrelated to the cover pool of the covered bond
the OTC derivative contract is not terminated in case of resolution or insolvency of the covered bond issuer or cover pool
the counterparty ranks at least pari passu with the covered bond holders except where the counterparty is the defaulting or the affected party, or waives the pari passu ranking
the OTC derivative contract is registered or recorded in the cover pool of the covered bond in accordance with national covered bond legislation
the derivative contract is used only to hedge the interest rate or currency mismatches of the cover pool in relation to the covered bond
the netting set does not include OTC derivative contracts unrelated to the cover pool of the covered bond
the covered bond to which the OTC derivative contract is associated meets the requirements of Articles 129(1), (2) and (3) of the CRR, and
the cover pool of the covered bond to which the derivative contract is associated is subject to a regulatory collateralisation requirement of at least 102 %

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 30a of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 Article 30a of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 A counterparty entering into an OTC hedging derivative contract with an SSPE may agree that VM is not posted by the SSPE, that VM is posted by the counterparty in the form of cash only, and that neither party posts IM, if:

core:listitem.core:para: the counterparty ranks at least pari passu with the holders of the most senior securitisation note, provided that counterparty is neither the defaulting nor the affected party
the SSPE is subject to a level of credit enhancement of the most senior securitisation note of at least 2% of the outstanding notes on an ongoing basis, and
the netting set does not include OTC derivative contracts unrelated to the securitisation

tr:secsub1.core:title: Exchange of collateral agreement
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 3 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 Counterparties who are subject to the margin requirements are required to enter into an exchange of collateral agreement which includes at least the following terms:

core:listitem.core:para: the levels and type of collateral required
collateral segregation arrangements
the netting set to which the exchange of collateral refers
the procedures for notification, confirmation and adjustment of margin calls
the procedures for settlement of margin calls for each type of eligible collateral
the procedures, methods, timeframes and allocation of responsibilities for the calculation of margins and the valuation of collateral
default and termination events
the law applicable to the non-centrally cleared OTC derivative contract, and
the law applicable to the exchange of collateral agreement

tr:secsub1.core:title: Collateral eligibility
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 4 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No.3) Instrument 2019Article 35A of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251. inserted by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure Regulation) (EU Exit) (No.5) Instrument 2020PRA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021FCA: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margining) Instrument 2021PRA Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margening) Instrument 2022FCA Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margening) Instrument 2022Collateral eligible to be used to comply with the margin requirements includes:

core:listitem.core:para: cash
debt securities issued by:

core:sub1listitem.core:para: until 31 March 2022: Member States’ and UK governments, central banks and public sector entities
from 1 April 2022: the UK government, BoE and UK public sector entities

core:listitem.core:para: debt securities issued by multi-lateral development agencies and international organisations
debt securities issued by credit institutions or investment firms
corporate bonds
the most senior tranches of securitisations
equities if they are included in a main index
shares or units in: UK UCITS, and

shares or units in funds which meet the criteria set out in Article 7(2)(b) of the Large Exposures (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook, provided that the conditions set out in Article 5A of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 (as amended by PRA Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margening) Instrument 2022 and FCA Standards Instrument: The Technical Standards (Bilateral Margening) Instrument 2022) are met

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 4 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No.3) Instrument 2019Concentration limits apply to collateral collected as IM.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Calculation of VM
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 11(2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Article 10 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 VM should be calculated daily on the basis of the mark to market values of the contracts in a specific netting set.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Calculation of IM
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 11(1) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251IM may be calculated using either or both:

core:listitem.core:para: Annex IV to Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 the standardised approach, or
Articles 14 to 18 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 an initial margin model

tr:secsub1.core:para: This is the most popular approach and it is anticipated that virtually all entities will use this approach. It may be different between counterparties and is a more bespoke approach.

In PRA CP13/23/FCA CP23/16—Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives: Amendments to BTS 2016/2251, the PRA and the FCA state that they propose not to implement a supervisory pre-approval requirement for using initial margin models. The PRA and FCA confirmed this approach in PRA PS18/23 FCA PS 23/19 Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives: Amendments to BTS 2016/2251.

Annex IV to Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251This is calculated as a percentage of the notional amount and is set out in Annex IV to the UK Margin RTS. This mirrors the mark-to-market approach set out in Articles 274 and 298 of the CRR. It is less flexible than the model approach and is likely to mean that the party posting collateral will have to post more collateral than if a model approach is used.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Segregation and treatment of IM
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 19(3) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251IM must be protected from the default or insolvency of the collecting counterparty by segregating it in either or both of the following ways:

core:listitem.core:para: on the books and records of a third-party holder or custodian
through other legally binding arrangements

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 19(4) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 Non-cash IM should be segregated as follows:

core:listitem.core:para: where collateral is held by the collecting counterparty on a proprietary basis, it should be segregated from the rest of the proprietary assets of the collecting counterparty
where collateral is held by the posting counterparty on a non-proprietary basis, it shall be segregated from the rest of the proprietary assets of the posting counterparty
where collateral is held on the books and records of a custodian or other third-party holder, it should be segregated from the proprietary assets of that third-party holder or custodian

tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 19(5) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 Where non-cash collateral is held by the collecting party or by a third-party holder or custodian, the collecting counterparty should provide the posting counterparty with the option to segregate its collateral from the assets of other posting counterparties.

Article 20 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 The collecting counterparty may not rehypothecate, repledge or otherwise reuse the collateral collected as IM, though a third-party holder may use IM received in cash for reinvestment purposes.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Timely confirmation
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 11(1)(a) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Articles 12(1) and (2) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013Non-centrally cleared OTC derivative contracts are required to be confirmed by the following deadlines:

core:listitem.core:para: contracts where each counterparty is an FC or NFC+—by the end of the business day following the date of execution
contracts where one counterparty is an NFC which is not an NFC+—by the end of the second business day following the date of execution
