tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 12(3) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013If a transaction is concluded after 16.00 local time, or with a counterparty located in a different time zone which does not allow confirmation by the set deadline, the confirmation shall take place as soon as possible and, at the latest, one business day following the applicable deadline.

Article 12(1) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013An OTC derivative contract should be confirmed, where available via electronic means. if a counterparty is able to justify that electronic confirmation is not available to it, for a variety of legitimate reasons, then confirmation may be performed by fax, paper, or manually processed emails.

Article 12(4) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013 as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No.2) Instrument 2019 (FCA 2019/62)FCs are required to report monthly to the FCA the number of unconfirmed OTC derivatives transactions that have been outstanding for more than five business days.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Portfolio reconciliation
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 13(3) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013Counterparties are required to reconcile their portfolios with the following frequencies:

core:listitem.core:para: FCs and NFC+s with 500 or more trades outstanding—daily
FCs and NFC+s with 51- 499 trades outstanding—weekly
FCs and NFC+s with 50 or less trades outstanding—quarterly
NFCs which are not NFC+s with more than 100 trades outstanding—quarterly
NFCs which are not NFC+s with 100 or less trades outstanding—yearly

tr:secsub1.core:title: Portfolio compression
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 14 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013Counterparties with 500 or more derivatives contracts outstanding that are not centrally cleared must have procedures in place to regularly (at least twice yearly) analyse the possibility of conducting a portfolio compression exercise. A portfolio compression exercise is an exercise in which two or more derivatives counterparties wholly terminate or change the notional value of some or all of the derivatives submitted by the counterparties for inclusion in the portfolio compression, primarily by terminating equal and offsetting trades, for the purposes of reducing counterparty risk, reducing fees associated with open positions and generally 'cleaning up' the relevant portfolio.

Article 14 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013Counterparties must be able to provide a reasonable explanation to their competent authority if they conclude that a portfolio compression exercise is not appropriate under the prevailing circumstances.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Dispute resolution
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 15(1) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013Counterparties must agree to detailed procedures and processes to identify, monitor and resolve disputes in a timely manner, with a specific process for disputes that are not resolved within five business days.

Article 15(2) of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013 as amended by the Technical Standards (European Market Infrastructure) (EU Exit) (No.2) Instrument 2019 (FCA 2019/62)FCs are required in addition to report to the FCA any disputes between counterparties relating to an OTC derivative contract, its valuation or the exchange of collateral for an amount or a value higher than €15m and outstanding for at least 15 business days.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Marking to market/marking to model
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 11(2) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Article 16 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013FCs and NFC+s are required to mark OTC derivatives to market on a daily basis unless market conditions such as market inactivity or unreliable pricing prevent marking-to-market, in which case a pricing model may be used.
Article 17 of Commission Delegated Assimilated Regulation (EU) 149/2013A pricing model should:

core:listitem.core:para: incorporate all factors that counterparties would consider in setting a price, including using as much marking-to-market information as possible
be consistent with accepted economic methodologies
be calibrated and tested for validity using prices from any observable market transactions
be validated and monitored independently by a division of the counterparty which is not the division taking the risk, and
be duly documented and approved by the board (or a board committee) of the counterparty at least annually

tr:secsub1.core:title: Capital
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 11(4) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012FCs are required to hold an appropriate and proportionate amount of capital to cover risks not covered by the exchange of collateral.
This general requirement is not supplemented by more detailed requirements in UK EMIR RTS.

tr:secsub1.core:title: Third country—counterparties
tr:secsub1.core:para: Article 11(12) of Assimilated Regulation (EU) 648/2012Additional risk mitigation requirements apply to OTC derivative contracts entered into between third-country entities that would be subject to those obligations if they were established in the UK, if:

core:listitem.core:para: the OTC derivative contracts have a direct, substantial and foreseeable effect within the UK, or
compliance with the requirements is necessary or appropriate to prevent the evasion of any provision of UK EMIR
